# Keeping CI fast and reliable

Treat feedback time, reliability and resource use as maintained requirements.
Every feature, dependency and test can change CI cost, even without a workflow
edit. AI agents and contributors should preserve useful coverage while reducing
unnecessary work, and leave failures easier to reproduce and diagnose.

This guide owns CI maintenance decisions and regression prevention. It does not
introduce another workflow, command catalog or acceptance policy.

| Question                                            | Authoritative owner                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Which tests, commands and CI jobs apply?            | [Testing feedback loop](testing-feedback-loop.md), owning `validation.json` contracts and [workflow definitions](../.github/workflows/) |
| What evidence permits acceptance or release?        | [Quality gates](quality-gates.md) and [version and release lifecycle](updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle)                       |
| Where does an implementation or shared rule belong? | [Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) and [script entry points](../scripts/README.md)                                                |
| Which consumers and documentation need updating?    | [Change alignment checklist](maintenance-checklist.md) and [documentation guidelines](DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md)                      |

Keep tool versions, matrix sizes, deadlines, cache keys and required-check names
in their existing executable owners. Keep run histories and investigation output
in ignored `tmp/` or PR/CI artifacts; durable decisions belong in the owning guide.

## Make the cost of a change explicit

Before adding a suite, fixture, dependency, platform or workflow, identify the
existing owner and the observable failure it must detect. Inspect the affected
plan and consumers through the [validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities).
Answer four questions in the change when they are material:

- What requirement needs new evidence, and why is existing evidence insufficient?
- Which layer and platform can exercise that requirement faithfully?
- What recurring setup, compilation, execution and artifact cost will it add?
- Can an existing task, fixture or compatible output supply it without weakening
  assertions or introducing another owner for the same rule?

Extend the existing implementation first. Share policy and lifecycle rules where
their meaning is identical; keep feature-specific fixtures local. An abstraction
is useful when it removes duplicated decisions and has clear inputs, outputs and
failure behavior. Avoid both copied shell fragments and a generic CI framework
whose configuration is harder to review than the work it coordinates.

Do not make a full local suite the default for every edit. Use affected feedback
while developing, then complete the applicable boundary and candidate gates.
New tests still need independent assertions; matching the implementation or
increasing a test count does not establish useful coverage.

## Keep workflow policy thin and reject cheap failures locally

Workflows own triggers, permissions, runners, matrices, dependencies and artifact
transport. Scripts own inventory validation, artifact roles, packaging, report
collection and execution policy. Reuse the same CLI locally and in Actions;
extract substantial conditionals and loops into the existing feature owner rather
than copying YAML fragments or introducing another generic orchestration layer.
When moving execution into a script, update every caller and smoke check. Keep
launcher behavior in its owning regression instead of requiring obsolete command
text in YAML. Cross-platform filesystem paths use `fileURLToPath` rather than
`.pathname`; ESM module arguments retain a file URL or relative module specifier
instead of a native Windows absolute path. Exercise each boundary on its platform.
Keep live source/release checks immediately before each publication boundary;
those protect against changed state and are not redundant setup checks.

The [syntax owner](../scripts/validation/syntax.mjs) parses changed Node, Bash and
Python sources without executing them or writing Python caches, and invokes
`actionlint` for changed workflows. Pre-commit selects staged paths but checks
worktree bytes, matching the existing structural checks. Affected validation also
checks new nonignored sources; PR creation checks the clean committed comparison.
Use Node 22, Bash and Python; install actionlint before changing workflows. No
checker installs tools or contacts the network. Hook installation configures hooks
without launching comprehensive health; request that gate explicitly.

PR creation runs `make pr-check`'s cheap-check owner against its actual comparison
base, rejects ownership blockers and checks applicable frontend patch coverage
before publication. Version projections, contract references and hygiene already
belong to structural standards; reuse that owner rather than adding duplicate
gates. Do not install dependencies, compile Rust, launch browsers or run application suites
implicitly in the cheap mode. Source changes during checking invalidate it.
Workflow edits also run the existing fast CI policy owner locally. Configuration
assertions and runner inventory discovery belong here; application execution and
native compiler fixtures do not. Keep static policy assertions independently runnable
without native tool setup. Scope fixture configuration changes to their owning
table or profile; repeated valid values elsewhere must remain unchanged. Update the existing policy assertion when its
requirement changes instead of adding a second overlapping test in another file.
Write generated reports into the task-owned evidence directory, not the source
checkout. Fixtures for source-integrity checks must preserve production ignore
rules; adding a fixture-only ignore can hide a real dirty-worktree failure.
For entry-point changes, also run the affected contract tests selected by the
existing validation plan before publication. A syntax pass or a hand-picked
filename sample cannot detect stale semantic routing expectations; cheap PR
checks do not certify those tests passed.

The frontend precheck reads the target from `codecov.yml`, includes partially
covered branches in the uncovered denominator and rejects omitted changed files.
Exercise report readers against actual producer output as well as small fixtures;
negative V8 branch counts remain uncovered rather than invalidating the report.
It verifies an existing clean-candidate `frontend-coverage` receipt through the
canonical stage owner and rechecks LCOV bytes, rather than trusting a timestamp or
raw report. Generate missing evidence explicitly with the reported command. A
verification-only miss never starts coverage, waits for a heavy lock or claims a
pass; a no-work verification lease must not imply admitted child work. Keep
verified scope termination diagnostics separate from the actual test result.
This frontend unit precheck is conservative; Rust and browser-union coverage
still need their owning evidence. Native execution, dependency resolution and
published-asset verification cannot be replaced by parsing or stale build output.

Use the existing package inventory's `frontendBuild` ownership when preparing
Rust selectors. Core, integrations and MCP selections still require real target
validation, but do not build frontend assets merely because Rust changed. Host
selections must still prepare Tauri's `frontendDist` before selector discovery.

Composed local gates must invoke shared stages through the same canonical command
and full-mode environment. Normalize `FAST=0` in both full-preflight children so
equivalent successful stages can reuse their verified receipts; do not weaken
identity checks or mutate the caller's environment to manufacture a cache hit.

Select local toolchain versions by prepending to the existing `PATH`; preserve
installed tools required by the repository's enabled Git hooks.

Local feedback does not replace committed-candidate acceptance. Git documents
that [hooks can be bypassed](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks); web edits and other
clients may not run them. Keep a compact authoritative remote check and necessary
runtime/native evidence. Delete duplicate execution only after comparing source,
configuration, platform, assertion and consumers, with an inventory/equivalence
control in the retained owner. The two optional-pack browser cases execute once
in full Linux Chromium; their separate job retains only its unique built-asset
and syntax checks. The non-instrumented ASan archive protocol executes once before
the required sanitizer producer, while actual instrumentation controls remain on
every consumer. Pure syntax does not establish either runtime contract.

Historical renderer, tray, window and network incident comparisons are manual
workflows. Their former development-branch bootstrap triggers do not provide
ordinary candidate acceptance. Keep their diagnostic tools available; normal
cross-platform native acceptance remains in the required backend caller. Review
all workflows, including scheduled, manual, reusable and publication roles, before
calling a job redundant merely because it is not a PR check.

## Measure the bottleneck before choosing the optimization

For a CI optimization task, use `gh` to collect the last 50 workflow runs and
their paginated, attempt-specific job and step records before editing workflows.
Keep successful, failed, cancelled and incomplete observations distinguishable.
For each job, separate dispatch/wait time, runner setup (checkout, tools,
dependencies, cache transfer and compilation) and test/check execution. Preserve
artifact/reporting overhead in the accounting rather than silently dropping it.
Where a step mixes compilation and tests, use its logs or Cargo timings and mark
any unresolved split as unknown. API dispatch timestamps can include `needs`
waits; they do not by themselves measure runner queue time.

For unexplained native-runner variation, retain comparable complete observations
and collect resource evidence before changing concurrency or compile profiles.
The existing native macOS coverage owner records CPU count, physical memory,
swap/VM snapshots and per-partition real/user/system time plus maximum
child RSS. A snapshot cannot prove peak memory pressure; maximum child RSS is
not concurrent compilers' aggregate peak. Preserve the original command status
and failure precedence, and keep diagnostics outside ordinary acceptance gates.
Keep detailed product tracing opt-in; routine resource measurements must not
enable per-operation traces merely to observe compiler behavior.

Use the existing [timing reports](testing-feedback-loop.md#measure-feedback-before-tuning-capacity).
Distinguish time to actionable feedback, time until required checks complete,
runner execution minutes and failure/rerun frequency. A change can improve one
while worsening another. Runner minutes are not billing, and a green rerun does
not erase the first failure.

Compare equivalent source changes, test inventories, platforms, toolchains and
cache conditions. Retain cold and warm observations, sample size, cancellations
and missing data. P50/P95 from a small or mixed historical sample are descriptive;
one faster run is not a durable latency guarantee. Job creation-to-start time can
include dependencies, so do not label it all runner queue time or call the last
finishing job a proven critical path.

| Observed cost               | Investigate first                                                                 | Prefer before adding capacity                                                        |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Waiting to start            | Actual dependency graph, runner availability, obsolete candidates, matrix fan-out | Remove unnecessary dependencies and safely cancel superseded verification            |
| Installation or compilation | Step timing, dependency graph, cache restore/save cost and compatibility          | Remove repeated setup and reuse compatible outputs; inspect Cargo timings            |
| Long test execution         | Slow cases, fixture preparation, worker saturation, shard imbalance               | Fix expensive setup and balance measured work within resource limits                 |
| Intermittent failures       | First failure logs, traces, readiness, task lifetime and leaked resources         | Reproduce and repair the owning fixture, product behavior or infrastructure          |
| Evidence collection         | Archive sizes, compression, transfer, merge and upload time                       | Produce each required report once and separate optional presentation from acceptance |

[Cargo build timings](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/timings.html)
help distinguish compilation work from test execution. A test scheduler cannot
remove compilation cost. Include dependency installation, archive transfer and
reporting in the comparison; moving cost into another job is not removing it.

Set latency and resource expectations from representative observations and the
purpose of each gate. A job timeout is a safety bound, not a performance target.
Record material budget changes and their rationale in the owning configuration
and review, rather than inventing universal minute limits in this guide.

Measure the complete unmutated baseline under its actual execution profile when
inventory or resource policy changes. Selected cases and tiny tool-contract
fixtures do not establish that the full cohort fits its per-case, suite and job
budgets. Preserve executed and unrun counts when fail-fast or a watchdog truncates
that evidence.

Budget a mutation chunk for the baseline obligation, every selected mutant's
build and complete consumer suite, setup and report publication. Do not assume
mutants fail early or reuse an old selected-count constant as the inventory grows.
The planner must preserve the rotating sample's exact union while bounding each
worker's work; a shorter chunk changes scheduling, not assurance coverage.
A shared baseline may remove repeated execution only when workers validate the
same run, source, tools, configuration, complete inventory and trusted producer
attempt through the existing evidence owner. Preserve raw tool reports: an
external baseline is separate verified evidence, never an invented tool outcome.
Failed-only reruns may reuse the attested successful producer attempt from the
same run; missing or mismatched evidence must fail before mutant execution.
Keep compilation, individual-test, complete-suite and job limits distinct and
reserve time for process retirement and evidence publication. Invoked tools may
create independent process groups; retain the real tool's cancellation and build
retirement controls, not only successful-run evidence. A closed supervisor pipe
cannot replace the actual work owner's acknowledgment. See
[actual work ownership](ai-coding-reliability.md#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime).

Stop an already failed candidate before starting another expensive compilation
partition. Linux/macOS native testing finishes all selected Host cases, then
admits the remaining complete workspace only if Host passed. Both partitions
still have to pass before reporting coverage; per-partition terminal result
collection, independent matrix jobs, default targets and zero retries remain
unchanged. The existing actual-tool coverage regression checks Host rejection,
remaining-partition rejection, successful coverage accumulation, timing pipelines
and report errors. Preserve partial backend evidence after a failure, while
requiring evidence on passing jobs; a producer skipped by an upstream failure
must not create a second missing-artifact error.

The [workspace coverage owner](../scripts/ci/workspace-coverage.sh) owns native
partition commands, timing pipelines and report generation; workflow steps pass
only the platform. Actual-tool failure controls verify both platform branches.

Keep complete tests distinct from duplicate instrumentation. macOS instruments
Host for its native desktop/updater branches, then runs every remaining default
workspace target with pinned Nextest without coverage instrumentation. Linux and
Windows retain full instrumented workspace coverage. This removes the separate
instrumented Core test build on Apple Silicon; it does not claim full macOS Core
line coverage. The actual-tool regression executes both workflow blocks, requires
all default targets and the Core execution marker, proves a clean macOS report
retains Host hits without a Core test cohort, and keeps both partition failures,
report failures, timing pipelines and process termination controls. All platform
assertions, doctests, zero retries and direct required checks remain unchanged.

A progressing serial test partition can exhaust its job watchdog without a hung
case. Windows reuses one sealed instrumented workspace archive across eight
independent serial consumers; every selected case still executes once with full
coverage, default targets, existing watchdogs and zero retries. Acceptance uses
those actual native checks directly. Do not add a second qualification workflow
or extend a job timeout to compensate for oversized units. Four extra setup and
archive transfers are a material cost; measure them alongside execution and runner
variation. The existing required-check owner retires old partition names only
after every current-source replacement passes with its bound app. Preserve strict
protection, unrelated checks and exact-source release acceptance together.

Treat a browser's total functional-case watchdog separately from its action,
assertion and product deadlines. A cold page, several successful state checks and
real interactions can cumulatively exhaust a short total bound without any one
operation failing. Full Chromium uses its existing Windows/coverage safety margin
on all hosts; portable execution retains its existing Windows allowance. Keep
state-based readiness, all assertions, explicit latency limits, zero retries and
first-failure traces. Do not erase a failed assertion by increasing its timeout.
The real-runner control derives both configured watchdogs, accelerates only their
duration, requires actual parked-case failure and subsequent-case execution, and
verifies descendant retirement before removing its fixture.


## Reuse compatible work with verifiable inputs

Prefer one producer for an expensive output when consumers need the same inputs
and artifact transfer is cheaper than rebuilding. Include the producer dependency
and its effect on parallelism in the measurement. Reuse compilation separately
from test execution: each required consumer still supplies its own assertions.
Keep production, coverage, sanitizer and mutation configurations distinct unless
their compatibility has been established.

Hosted Ubuntu Rust jobs prepare disk capacity before restoring Cargo outputs.
The [runner storage owner](../scripts/ci/runner-storage.mjs) reclaims only three
fixed unused SDK directories from disposable image contents and reports actual
free bytes before and after. Each heavy job uploads that small measurement before
cache expansion, so a later exhausted runner does not erase the preparation evidence.
It preserves the workspace, build caches and tools
used by compilation and analysis; local/self-hosted contexts and redirected paths
are not cleanup targets. Its real filesystem controls cover preservation and
idempotence. Inspect those measurements and cache expansion before responding
to disk exhaustion; a failed runner may be unable to upload its own logs.

A cache is an optional accelerator. A cold or evicted cache must still allow
correct execution. Measure restored bytes, restore/save time, useful hits and
eviction; a reported hit alone does not prove a faster build. Preserve the
existing trust boundaries and write policy. GitHub documents cache matching,
branch access and eviction in its [dependency caching reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching).

Prefer setup actions' built-in dependency caching: configure `setup-node` for
npm and the actual lockfiles; `setup-go` normally enables its cache by default;
use `Swatinem/rust-cache` for compatible Rust outputs. Check the repository's
current cache allowance and usage before adding archives. Keep a frontend-only
job free of Cargo cache restoration, and do not cache installed outputs that are
cheaper to recreate than transfer. A cache key must describe compatible inputs,
not merely create more apparent hits. Avoid publishing identical archives from
every shard; preserve trusted write policy and existing producer ownership.

An exact cache hit is immutable: it cannot acquire newly needed dependency
feature/profile variants after a workflow changes its compilation cohorts.
Review that transition explicitly; rotate only the affected platform's cache
epoch when needed, preserving trusted writes. A new prefix has a real initial
cold-build cost and competes with the old entry for the repository allowance.
Do not enable workspace-crate caching or add per-commit keys merely to hide a
slow build. Distinguish dependency reuse from the workspace source that must
still compile; a cache repair does not explain unrelated runner variability.

Download pinned prebuilt development tools through the existing installer where
available. Verify support in the repository-pinned installer version; an unknown
tool can select an unintended source-build or registry fallback. Bind direct
release downloads to a reviewed digest and execute the installed version check.
Compiling tools with `go install` or `cargo install` is recurring setup
work; retain source installation only when the required tool has no suitable
trusted binary or the test explicitly validates its build.

Build twice consecutively with identical source, profile, features and environment.
Inspect unexpected second-build work before enlarging caches or runner counts:
missing `rerun-if-changed` inputs, generated files that change every invocation,
unnecessary frontend rebuilds, and container layers that copy source before
installing locked dependencies. A bundler may intentionally rebuild quickly;
judge the observed cost instead of requiring it to behave like Cargo's no-op build.

Auxiliary diagnostic transport must not decide test acceptance or skip later
independent checks after an artifact-service outage. Keep test execution, local
result publication and required cleanup fatal; only the reviewed upload step is
best-effort. The CI policy owner enumerates these roles: Health logs and raw
coverage copies, storage measurements, crash/timing diagnostics, optional HTML
and failure attachments. Source-bound coverage maps, partition archives/unions,
native/backend and release/security evidence stay mandatory. A missing automatic
consumer alone does not make an artifact optional: authoritative human reports
and manual diagnostic deliverables can still require it. Do not retry tests to
repair transport, or suppress the original failed attempt.

An artifact used as acceptance evidence has a stronger contract. Its consumer
must validate the actual tested head or merge source, workflow/run/attempt, platform and architecture,
relevant toolchain/features, expected inventory and content digests required by
the owning protocol. A matching filename, a successful download or a cache hit
is insufficient. Digests detect content changes; provenance establishes whether
those bytes belong to the intended candidate. Reject missing, stale, duplicate,
partial or incompatible inputs before merging evidence.

Keep these checks in the existing producer/consumer owner. Do not add a second
receipt format or evidence resolver. Exercise rejected-input cases when changing
that boundary, and preserve the documented rerun procedure for attempt-bound
artifacts. GitHub's download action reports a digest mismatch as a warning;
the evidence consumer must explicitly reject it. See [artifact validation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/store-and-share-data#validating-artifacts)
for the platform behavior.

## Refactor coverage without losing its meaning

Two executions are redundant only when their requirement, inputs, platform and
evidence obligations are equivalent. A browser mock, real desktop process,
encrypted loopback exchange and physical network observation prove different
things. Keep the [platform evidence boundaries](platform-validation.md).

Before merging or deleting a check, map each assertion and downstream consumer
to its retained owner. Update affected selectors, fixtures, artifact consumers,
required checks and release consumers together where applicable. Validate the
replacement on the current candidate before the existing protected obligation
can be retired under the [quality gates](quality-gates.md). Eliminate redundant
aggregate jobs when direct checks provide the required enforcement; retain a
collector when it actually validates completeness or combines required evidence.

Selection and sharding need inventories, not just successful exit codes. Verify
that required cases are present, partitions are complete and disjoint where
intended, and expected platform-specific or ignored cases remain explicit.
Empty selections, skipped dependencies and incomplete collectors cannot stand in
for executed coverage. Moving Rust execution to another runner must also retain
separately owned doc-tests and integration/ignored-test obligations.

Use [same-source selection audits](testing-feedback-loop.md#qualify-affected-selection-alongside-full-gates)
before proposing narrower gates. Imports alone cannot reveal every runtime,
native or generated consumer. Moving a check from PRs to a schedule changes
detection latency and acceptance scope; describe and review that tradeoff rather
than calling it equivalent coverage delivered faster.

Workflow path filters and job conditions have different required-check behavior.
GitHub warns that a workflow skipped by path or branch filtering can leave its
required check pending; a skipped job can report success. A collector must still
run when a dependency fails and explicitly reject failed, cancelled, missing or
unexpectedly skipped required work. Use `!cancelled()` for verification collector jobs: it permits explicit rejection
after upstream failure, but releases superseded workflows on cancellation. An
unconditional `always()` collector can remain queued after its producers are
cancelled and hold the concurrency group needed by the latest candidate. Keep
necessary resource cleanup independent. The scheduling condition does not
validate dependencies; the collector must still inspect every required result. See [required-check troubleshooting](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks).

Before adding docs-only path filters, inspect actual branch protection and the
app-bound checks it requires, including external coverage and security checks.
Define which documentation is inert: generated help, executable examples, eval
prompts, fixtures and policy inputs can change product or acceptance behavior.
Keep applicable documentation checks. Use workflow-level filters only when no
required consumer will wait for their missing result. A lightweight selection or
collector job must retain the required check identity and reject failed selection;
it must not fabricate coverage or security results belonging to another app.
Codecov provides a native [empty upload](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-cli#empty-upload)
for diffs it classifies as ignored; never force it for an ineligible diff. Qualify
the current-SHA provider result before relying on it. This does not replace real
CodeQL analysis or establish that documentation cannot affect product inputs.
GitHub evaluates [job conditions before matrix expansion](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_idif):
a skipped matrix job does not prove that every expanded required context exists.
Inspect actual returned names and app IDs before narrowing protected work.
Preserve complete main-commit verification required by release consumers even
when a PR has a separately validated docs-only path.

The UI HTML collector follows the mandatory full-shard producers, independently
of the optional extended-browser jobs. If Health prevents desktop shards from
starting, their missing reports remain incomplete evidence. The collector checks
all platform-specific current-attempt shards (eight macOS, four Linux/Windows); fixing the upstream failure and rerunning
the selected producers supplies that evidence, rather than omitting those OSes.

## Documentation-only PR scope

The [scope owner](../scripts/ci/docs-scope.mjs) permits a fast path only for
same-repository PRs targeting `main` whose exact tested merge changes ordinary
README or documentation prose. It reads the NUL-delimited Git delta, including
file modes, and reuses the validation contracts to exclude owned inputs and
authority references. Help, evaluation prompts, policy guides, executable or
symlink changes, deletions, renames, mixed code changes and uncertain inputs do
not qualify. Fork PRs retain full coverage because the coverage provider's empty
upload does not have the ordinary tokenless fork authentication guarantee.

Required matrix identities remain present. Their jobs independently verify the
selection, use Ubuntu for the documentation path, and describe product tests as
not applicable rather than executed. Nonrequired heavy producers can be skipped;
full-scope collectors still require their original exhaustive, source-bound
artifacts. Do not manufacture empty execution receipts or coverage files. A failed
selector must fail required jobs even when dependency scheduling would otherwise
skip them. Defaults for standalone, scheduled and manual callers require full work.

The documentation path retains whitespace, structural ownership and hygiene
checks through their existing owners. Ubuntu source formatting, spelling, workflow
lint and supply-chain scans remain enabled. Real CodeQL, secret scanning,
dependency review and lightweight mutation-runner contracts remain enabled.
Codecov uses its native, unforced empty-upload operation; an accepted HTTP request
does not prove a passing provider check. Verify the actual current-head App check.
No broad coverage ignore rule or replacement provider status is needed.
Pin the downloaded CLI independently of the Action commit: an Action pin can
still resolve a moving `latest` tool. Keep ordinary and empty-upload clients
aligned and retain the provider's integrity verification.

Use a shallow checkout containing the merge and both parents; full ancestry is
unnecessary for this exact base-to-merge comparison. Missing objects, mismatched
source or failed output publication cannot authorize skipped work. The real Git
fixtures retain positive depth-two and negative missing-history, mode, authority,
fork and mixed-change controls. Run these and the workflow policy locally before
publication, then qualify actual required names and skipped work in a real docs PR.

Every main push, merge group, schedule and manual run retains full verification.
Release acceptance binds checks to the latest successful trusted main-push run
and its owning workflow suite; a successful PR scope decision is not release
evidence, even at the same source SHA. Add this provenance requirement without
removing the existing veto from newer failed or pending required checks.
[Quality gates](quality-gates.md) owns
acceptance and [updates](updates.md) owns publication requirements.

## Bound parallelism and preserve isolation

Run independent checks in parallel, but inspect each `needs` edge before removing
it: artifact availability, coverage provenance and deliberate runner admission
are real dependencies even when no explicit job output is passed. Put portable
formatting, source lint and dependency auditing on Ubuntu. Retain macOS/Windows
execution when assertions exercise their native behavior. 
... command output truncated for persistence ...
ll. Such a path also needs R01–R03. Budget values remain in the
[network contracts](network-design-reference.md#8-resource-budgets-compatibility-and-performance)
and implementation, rather than a second set of constants here.

**Evidence:** stall admission and a later network phase separately, use multiple
candidate routes, and verify permits/socket owners are released. Check that an
expired preflight has no partial durable mutation. Examples live in
[privacy runtime tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/privacy_runtime_tests.rs)
and [group invitation tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests.rs).

## R05: Bounded work must also make progress

**Failure pattern:** taking the first N entries every turn permanently excludes
older pending work; failed items pin a cursor; unbounded retries flood a queue;
or a completion signal arrives between checking a condition and registering a
waiter, leaving work asleep indefinitely.

Review fairness across successive turns, not only the batch size. Use the existing
cursor, coalescing and admission owners; distinguish independent lanes where
needed. Failed publication must not indefinitely prevent later eligible work.
Recheck conditions with the synchronization primitive's correct waiter protocol;
a notification alone is not the durable condition. Admission must observe both
permit release and transitions that make retained resources reclaimable. A one-time
pressure check can miss a busy connection becoming idle after the waiter starts.
The [session pool](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/session_pool.rs) owns this
handoff: idle eligibility requests retirement, while the actual connection keeps
its permits until destruction. Preserve startup, wake,
shutdown and missed-notification recovery behavior.
Delivery fixtures reuse the register-before-check durable-status observer in
[delivery runtime tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/delivery_runtime_tests.rs),
not periodic polling that competes with protocol and persistence workers. Keep
the exact message predicate and original deadline; the late exact-receipt
regression rejects unrelated wakeups, and the oversized-message regression also
retains pre-acceptance rejection and unchanged ratchet state.

Keep independent reasons for continuing work separate. A worker can finish a
history page and then fail an optional favorites exchange; reporting that error
must not discard unfinished history or a refresh received during the exchange.
Consume a coalesced wake only when its follow-up remains scheduled after every
error branch. A failure without pending work must still avoid a busy retry loop.

Retain demand throughout backoff. A future retry deadline makes queued work
temporarily ineligible; it does not consume that work. Wake the existing scheduler
at the earliest retained deadline when a worker is available, without relying on
periodic repair. A queued deadline must not spin while its worker is occupied.
The `account_history_capacity_backoff_retains_demand_without_periodic_repair`
regression in [account sync tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/selection_tests.rs)
checks real admission contention, retained work and the unchanged backoff.

Keep count, byte, task and concurrency budgets intact. Fair scheduling does not
guarantee a successful write into a full store, justify eviction of durable intent
or permit increasing capacity without reviewing consumers.

Finite preparation must survive unrelated ordinary appends without relaxing its
authority fences. Compare the owner's complete control and destructive revisions;
an unfinished derived index cannot certify a concurrent append. Capture completed
index readiness so later turns can progress. The ordinary-append and pending
observation regressions in [participant network selection](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/privacy_sync/network.rs)
exercise progress alongside capability, proof, roster and file-policy invalidation.

**Evidence:** create more eligible items than one batch, put pending work behind
terminal history, and include a failed item, cancellation and newly arriving work.
Assert progress and budget preservation across turns. See publication rotation
tests in the [group journal](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/operations/journal.rs).
The `account_history_after_favorites_*` regressions in
[account sync tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/selection_tests.rs)
cover successful and failed optional exchanges, retained refreshes, unfinished
history pages and failure without pending work.

## R06: Exact authority and stale completions

**Failure pattern:** work authorized before an await or queue delay commits after
logout, same-user relogin, account replacement or a policy off/on transition.
Comparing only the username or current Boolean value misses changed authority.

Capture the owner's exact session/runtime installation and relevant revision at
entry. Revalidate through the existing atomic commit seam before side effects
and before publishing private results. Treat frontend generation guards as UI
ownership, not host authorization. Read commands can expose stale private data too.

A routing or capability preview must not become a second admission owner. When
the canonical reader reports a typed stale projection, preserve its existing
bounded preparation path before deciding authorization. Any cached local candidate
still needs full identity and current authority checks at the real commit seam.
The [forwarding owner](message-forwarding.md#source-admission-and-lifecycle) tests a
signed rename that needs preparation, plus dissolution and same-user/different-key
controls that must never produce a message or send receipt.

Account for reentrant store subscribers and callbacks that can retire an owner
synchronously during publication. Lock once when combining sensitive proof and
revision checks. If a guard must be released around preparation, reacquire it and
check all invalidating conditions; an earlier successful check is insufficient.
Compensation must identify the stale operation's own effects and must not erase
newer valid state.

Scope presentation readiness and failure flags to the resource that produced
them, too. A component-wide decode failure can suppress a replacement image,
and a retired load callback can publish stale geometry. The
[inline media owner](module-boundaries.md#inline-media-presentation) binds both
outcomes to the current URL and session; the replacement-source and retired-load
regressions in [MediaPreview tests](../frontend/src/features/chat/MediaPreview.test.ts)
exercise recovery and rejection of stale callbacks.

**Evidence:** pause at the real commit seam; replace the session with the same
owner, change the relevant policy revision, or remove the source; then resume.
Assert no stale mutation or plaintext publication, plus a valid positive path.
The [desktop session owner](module-boundaries.md#2-feature-owners-and-shared-decisions)
and [runtime admission](../src-tauri/src/runtime_admission.rs) define the shared seam.

## R07: Observation is not mutation ownership

**Failure pattern:** a never-settling read leaves the UI busy forever; a timeout
is treated as failed durable mutation; clearing a busy flag allows duplicate
submission while the original native write continues; optional hydration hides
a known successful commit.

Use existing bounded read/observation helpers, retire stale listeners/timers and
offer a recoverable UI state. Preserve the actual mutation's ownership, ordering
and exact operation ID until its real outcome is known. Unknown admission must
remain unknown; reconcile or retry according to the owning idempotency contract.
Process a late definite refusal without fabricating a protocol terminal state.
Do not turn failed readback into an empty successful save or resend an accepted
message because optional roster, preview or notification work failed.

**Evidence:** hold IPC unresolved beyond the observation deadline, attempt a
duplicate action, then settle the original call with success and with refusal in
separate cases. Switch sessions during the wait. Assert bounded UI observation,
no overlapping mutation and correct late settlement. See
[group operation tests](../frontend/src/store/accountGroupOperations.test.ts),
[outgoing intent tests](../frontend/src/store/outgoingIntent.test.ts) and
[coordinated state owners](module-boundaries.md#coordinated-state-owners).

## R08: Durable state and failure semantics

**Failure pattern:** a read-modify-write race loses another update; optimistic
success precedes durable acceptance; retries duplicate writes; a failed/corrupt
read is silently treated as empty state; cleanup after a partial failure destroys
recoverable user data.

Identify the commit point, serialization owner and restart/replay behavior.
Prepare expensive work separately, then compare expected revision and lifetime
under the owning commit guard. Preserve operation IDs, ordering, atomic replacement
and existing compatibility rules. Multi-store changes are not automatically one
transaction; define recovery or compensation for every partial commit boundary.
Use established error types and distinguish absent, unavailable and corrupt data.

Preserve accepted intent when presentation fails. Report what actually committed;
do not relabel a committed change as rejected because later best-effort work
failed. Avoid empty catches, blanket defaults or unconditional retries that hide
the distinction. Follow the owning feature guide for rollback and durability.

**Evidence:** fail before and after the commit point, interleave a second writer,
retry with the same identity, and restart using retained data. Verify acknowledged
state survives, stale cleanup cannot delete a newer write, and partial outcomes
are reported honestly. See [development conventions](../specifications/development_conventions.md)
and the feature-specific owners in [module ownership](module-boundaries.md).

## R09: Bound input and resource use

**Failure pattern:** peer/UI-controlled data expands into unbounded allocation,
recursive traversal, decode work, fanout or task creation; a file path crosses its
allowed namespace; a convenient new IPC endpoint bypasses the existing admission
or authorization owner.

Validate at the owning trust boundary before allocation and side effects, using
existing frame, file, count, depth and byte limits. Preserve exact account/device
bindings and path/consent checks. Display metadata and frontend validation are
not authorization. Bound queues and retained retry state as well as active work;
do not remove backpressure to make a benchmark look faster.

**Evidence:** test the limit and just beyond it, malformed or missing data,
wrong-owner requests, saturation and recovery after capacity returns. Include
real loopback assertions for changed networking/crypto boundaries as required by
the [network review matrix](network-design-reference.md#minimum-feature-review-matrix).
Physical execution resources need the same ownership discipline. A hosted runner
can exhaust disk while expanding a cache or compiling a second profile, before
it can publish failure logs. The [runner storage owner](../scripts/ci/runner-storage.mjs)
measures real capacity and reclaims only fixed disposable image SDK payloads;
[its filesystem controls](../scripts/diagnostics/runner-storage.test.mjs) protect
workspace/toolchain data, redirected paths and non-hosted environments.
Keep secrets and private payloads out of diagnostic logs and fixtures.

## R10: Evidence that exercises the failure

Scope fixture transformations and assertions to the owning configuration table,
not globally unique text. Test the same valid value in an unrelated profile and
verify that it stays unchanged. The [Nextest fixture owner](../scripts/diagnostics/test-fixtures/nextest.mjs)
and [cheap CI policy regressions](../scripts/diagnostics/ci-latency.test.mjs)
protect this boundary; actual compiler fixtures still exercise native behavior.

Source-integrity fixtures must not ignore tool output that production leaves
untracked. Keep generated evidence outside the source checkout and assert the
checkout stays clean after real tool execution; also prove unrelated untracked
source is still rejected. The [shared mutation controls](../scripts/release/run-mutants.test.mjs)
own this regression without weakening the production cleanliness gate.

Keep unrelated tool-version startup outside process-lifecycle assertions. The
[supervisor isolation regression](../scripts/diagnostics/windows-process-owner.test.mjs)
uses the existing version fixture while retaining real stage and output-limit
children, original watchdogs and verified completion receipts. Confirm the probes
were used; do not replace the process behavior under test. Check nested budgets
before treating an outer timeout as evidence that the inner operation hung.

Check name, App identity and source SHA alone do not establish execution scope.
A documentation eligibility decision is not product-test evidence, even when its
required job succeeds. Consumers must also validate the event, trusted repository,
branch and owning workflow/run. The release source owner binds checks to the
latest successful main-push suite; its PR-only, wrong-owner and stale-success
controls prevent a lightweight decision from authorizing publication.
Provenance is an additional constraint: filtering to a trusted suite must not
discard a newer failed or pending check that previously blocked acceptance.

Process-lifecycle fixtures must distinguish leader exit from group signal
permission. Observe the fixture-owned leader's process state when synchronizing

that leader is still running. The escaped inherited-output-pipe cases in

Source-order contracts must assert that each required command exists before
comparing its position. A missing substring returns a sentinel such as `-1` and
can otherwise make an ordering assertion pass vacuously. Match the canonical

Negative controls must prove their intended input reached that boundary. For Git
scope tests, assert the real path and mode; a host that ignores executable bits
can otherwise produce an empty delta whose rejection passes the wrong assertion.

Browser fixtures must make hydrated backend settings agree with the intended

For saved reading positions, exhausting bounded animation-frame polling does not
prove geometry is ready: retain the conversation-owned target and resume on
geometry changes, cancelling observers on cleanup and reader intent. The viewport

Raw storage injection in concurrency fixtures must publish through the normal
owner notification before requiring a peer's unrelated scope to settle. Preserve
the protected in-flight page, exact inventory assertions and original latency
bounds; the same-source control fixture owns this preparation contract. Finish
unrelated readiness preparation before dispatching a timed network read. A
protected task can still reach its genuine idle deadline. Test barriers belong
before I/O, inside the owned child, with cancellation releasing their futures;
post-send hooks must not hide that deadline. Do not repeat long preparation waits
inside the measured held-read window.

Concurrent actual-tool fixtures must own output directories, not only source
and temporary data. A second Playwright invocation can otherwise clean a running
suite's traces. The browser command owner retains live logs and case progress,
joins descendants before reporting and fails on timeout or uncertain retirement.

Keep a test's observation scope equal to its named requirement. The
growing-history fixture measures exact durable originals during continuation,
then checks the full public
projection after retiring its continuously appending peers. Its projection read
must not compete with an endless writer inside the continuation latency bound.
Paused-clock maintenance tests wait for actual retry attempts and assert minimum
backoff spacing; real measured database duty time cannot imply a fixed number of
attempts inside an arbitrary virtual-time window. Preserve cancellation, other
maintenance-class progress and the no-early-retry assertions.

Prefer one qualified scenario for a requirement over repeated whole-host
variants with weaker preparation. The same-source control receipt owner retains
its five prepared partial-corpus Noise scenarios, including the exact live child
at admission, both preserved checkpoints, unchanged eight-second receipt,
cancellation and post-release recovery. Its former empty-corpus duplicate could
lose a natural read between setup notification and admission; removing that
variant does not qualify a separate fresh empty-corpus timing boundary. Keep the
retired-child observer and interrupted-preparation controls rather than adding
sleep, suppressing publication or accepting a stale child to rescue setup.
Its test-only dispatch gate must classify the actual owed parked pair credit,
not the shared resumed trace label. Capture that one-shot child before waiting
for its later projection; retain exact private-receipt evidence before release.
The paid-pair classifier regression rejects foreground resumes and unprotected
turns while the real Noise scenarios retain admission and recovery assertions.
When inventory ordering selects a different continuation path, construct canonical
signed fixture events with noncolliding deterministic identifiers and assert the
actual persisted key ordering. Distinguish durable commit, completed publication
and recipient installation in timing evidence; a publication-begin trace is not
proof of completion. Preserve bounded owner-phase diagnostics through recovery
without extending the measured deadline or warming away the required cold work.

A progressing serial test partition can exhaust its job watchdog without a hung
case. The Windows archive owner uses eight native serial execution partitions,
with direct required checks and the existing sealed once-only inventory contract.
Exercise actual pinned archive consumers and omission/duplication/failed-execution
controls. Preserve watchdogs, product assertions and full coverage. The existing
protection migration owner requires every successful current-head app-bound
replacement before retiring oversized partition names; skipped or partial runs
cannot qualify. Account for additional archive/setup cost and hosted variation.
The shared union verifier takes the caller-owned partition count; Windows capacity
changes must not alter the independent eight-part ASan contract. Run both real-tool
protocol fixtures and their missing/duplicate/failed-receipt controls. ASan
compilation reuse must bind the source, platform, compiler and archive/manifest
digests through trusted producer outputs. Reject changed bytes and inventories
before running archived tests; fresh-consumer controls must prove execution
without producer build outputs. Retain real instrumentation checks on each runner.

A total functional browser-case watchdog is not a product performance SLA.
Trace the failed interval: when several individually successful cold-load,
rendering and interaction steps exhaust the total, use the existing generous
functional allowance consistently across platforms. Preserve individual
assertion bounds and explicit latency contracts. The real Playwright watchdog
control derives the actual source configuration, accelerates only its duration,
and requires timeout failure plus later-case execution with joined descendants;
never disable the watchdog or use retries to qualify a failure.

Independent message kinds should have independent browser scenarios. The
[automatic delivery fixture](../frontend/e2e/automatic-delivery.spec.ts) checks
text, sticker and file-card Awaiting/explicit projection separately; keep the
file disclosure and keyboard assertions in its file case. Three unrelated send
journeys can exhaust one functional watchdog before their final assertion.
Update the authoritative browser inventory alongside the split, retaining strict
trace/error evidence and every kind's confirmation predicate.

Functional browser scenarios should use the smallest data set that exercises
all named state transitions. Recovery-batch navigation needs distinct partial
and terminal deliveries plus concurrent live and duplicate signals; repeated
extra rows only multiply traced render work. Keep the separate large-history
window case and deterministic announcement-coalescing/deduplication tests in
[conversation reception](group-conversation-reception.md).

Use barriers, deferred promises, injected provider/storage stalls and controlled
clocks at the actual boundary. Prefer an observable progress assertion to an
arbitrary sleep or a test that checks only that a timeout helper was called.
Verify successful behavior, failure, cleanup and replacement through the same
production owner; a mock that bypasses the problematic lock proves little.

The group-inventory held-peer fixture rejects a real authenticated setup
exchange before admitting its independent publication measurement. Snapshot
exact-peer/group begin and end counters only after the actual Fingerprint hold
enters; require exactly one live round, unchanged counters and an open transport
through the original eight-second publication bound. A setup failure is not a
measured-window completion. A server task parked after client EOF is not a live
hold; observe transport retirement and join it on cancellation. The owner is
`group_inventory_publication_progresses_while_unrelated_peer_sync_is_held` in
`account_documents/tests.rs`, selected by core-account-group validation.

Give connection setup and capability negotiation their own bounded watchdog.
Start a progress deadline only after the required stalled operation is admitted,
and prove the competing work is still incomplete at that point. Release only
that work's barrier while retaining the stall. Measure cancellation separately
from setup and history progress; preserve each behavior's required bound.

A periodic probe can miss readiness between its last check and the deadline.
Use [R05](#r05-bounded-work-must-also-make-progress)'s waiter protocol to recheck
the actual condition on a transition, retaining the original deadline and bounded
fallback. A snapshot taken after timeout is diagnostic evidence, not success.

An offline fixture that needs prompt connection failure must own and observe
actual transport closure; reserving a TCP port does not guarantee refusal or
retire a pending dial. The [own-copy fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/delivery_runtime_tests.rs)
qualifies real accept-and-close behavior, joins its unavailable-endpoint owner,
then hands the same listener to the cold application without changing its
confirmation budget.

A direct protocol fixture must own its cold-start preconditions. Starting every
background repair loop can negotiate or import the claimed first request before
the explicit operation and consume its transport capacity. Reuse the bounded
[inbound connection owner](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/serving.rs) when the
scenario drives requests directly; keep full-host recovery tests separate. The
[certificate refresh fixture](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/tests.rs)
requires no prior sibling negotiation or imported custody key, then positively
witnesses its real explicit negotiation and durable projection. It commits its
baseline without fanout and explicitly drives each real sync/Have exchange before
observing custody. A passive observer cannot advance pending work when the
fixture deliberately has no autonomous recovery owner.

Keep fixture validation at the narrow boundary it owns. A full-host scenario
whose only assertion concerns another test helper adds unrelated synchronization
and scheduling prerequisites without a product oracle. Reuse the real protocol
and business scenarios instead: [Wake authentication and recovery controls](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/selection_tests.rs)
own linked identity, revision deduplication and notification-driven convergence;
[custody scenarios](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_documents/tests.rs)
own authenticated preparation, held-domain independence and durable custody.
Custody accounting preparation uses serial real channel-document requests on
inbound-only peers before autonomous workers start. A mutable whole-Optional or
Wake-settled snapshot is not a prerequisite for that accounting contract: it can
restart and create unrelated capacity contention while an observer waits. Remove
the global observer and its helper-only full-host tests; retain signed channel
floors, exact-peer capabilities and the real automatic custody/offline controls.
Do not add a clock switch solely to rescue a helper's self-test. Keep a loopback
business scenario focused on its named behavior. The member-invitation proof
ends after epoch delivery, pre-join isolation and role rejection. Existing
focused transfer/authority controls own ownership changes; the small two-node
departure proof owns actual offline pause/relaunch and retry of the original
signed event and parent cut. Do not chain unrelated controls and reconnection
requirements onto an already complete invitation scenario.

A fixture with a live authoritative identity observer must not simulate account
replacement by changing only a derived UI store. A later valid backend observation
can restore that store. Keep the [startup browser proof](../frontend/e2e/theme-picker.spec.ts)
focused on startup and real logout/relogin; the [scoped pack](../frontend/src/store/packs.test.ts)
and [linked appearance](../frontend/src/lib/linkedAppearance.test.ts) controls own
replacement and stale callbacks. A browser test of an actual account transition
must change its authoritative identity boundary consistently.

Keep a scheduling control's corpus at the protocol boundary it needs. The
[queued-source controls](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests/selected_queued_source_control_latency.rs)
use a normal short partial page and retain strict result/checkpoint ordering;
separate real-protocol tests own full-page durability and replay. Qualify request
liveness before its cancellation trigger and the actual resumed owner before
admission. A cancellation-triggering publication need not leave the old request
alive after the publisher returns.

Browser device options express intent; they do not observe native input state.
Establish the required device mode through the browser's supported emulation
owner, then verify actual media queries and touch capabilities before measuring
responsive hit areas. Do not replace `matchMedia` with a JavaScript mock. The
[touch fixture](../frontend/e2e/touch-targets.spec.ts) exercises controlled native
state loss, actual CSS target sizes and a real tap through that same owner.
A negative control must observe the capability it removes; disabling touch does
not require every host to become hover-capable or shrink its CSS targets.

A deadlock regression must not hang its own runner: bound coordination, arrange
fixture release even when assertions fail, and use an isolated process with an
outer deadline when a synchronous lock cycle cannot be safely unwound. An async
timeout inside the blocked thread is not sufficient. Avoid port-selection races
and process-global fixtures that assume serial execution; respect the repository's
test environment and resource controls.

Intentional cancellation and output-limit controls need an independent process
owner. Inheriting the real runner's owner marker can terminate the enclosing
validation instead of only the synthetic command. The
[process-owner fixture](../scripts/diagnostics/windows-process-owner.test.mjs)
checks both the retained output-limit failure and successful enclosing supervisor
through an actual nested execution.

Executable process fixtures must copy their image and assert independent file
identity; a hard link aliases the live harness outside the child process owner.
The process-owner and release-reuse fixtures share bounded filesystem cleanup
after verified retirement, with a Windows held-image control that still rejects
a persistent lock and succeeds only after release.

Treat a lock-order suspicion, a reproduced bug and a passing regression as
different evidence. A stack sample or total suite duration alone does not prove
one test is deadlocked. Inspect the active operation, its duration and the actual
wait dependencies. Preserve required assertions when fixing flaky setup; do not
hide a failure with retries, larger sleeps, skipped tests or weaker selectors.

Record the tested source, command, environment, count and outcome. Reassess
consumers after merging new callers or changing a shared helper. Static scans,
passing unit tests and browser IPC mocks do not establish native OS behavior or
the absence of every deadlock. Cancelled, interrupted, empty and unavailable runs
remain distinct from passes. Completed individual commands do not turn a cancelled
parent run into a passing full gate. Verification collectors must release cancelled workflows while still rejecting
upstream failures. An unconditional collector can retain a cancelled candidate
and block its replacement in the concurrency group. The
[CI maintenance guide](ci-maintenance.md) owns this scheduling rule;
[merge-queue regressions](../scripts/diagnostics/merge-queue.test.mjs) exercise
eligibility after failure and ineligibility after cancellation. Follow the
[validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
and keep unresolved native, cross-platform and stress obligations explicit.

## Review record

For applicable risks, make these answers reviewable in the PR or task result:

- **Owner and invariant:** which implementation and authoritative rule apply?
- **Risks:** which rule IDs apply, and what reachable failure path was checked?
- **Progress and lifetime:** what can wait, what stays available, and who owns work
  after cancellation, retirement or retry?
- **Commit and authority:** what becomes durable, what invalidates permission,
  and how are stale or partially completed effects handled?
- **Evidence:** which regression/scenario exercised the boundary on which source,
  and what actually passed, failed or remained unverified?

Use concrete paths, operations and assertions. “Thread safe,” “handles errors,”
“tests pass” and checked boxes without evidence are not sufficient explanations.
For a nonapplicable risk, a short reason is enough; do not manufacture tests or
ceremonial reports for unrelated concerns.

## Keep the guide useful as defects are found

The author of a confirmed defect fix owns the corresponding guidance update;
the reviewer checks it alongside the regression and owning contract. Follow the
[requirement maintenance loop](testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

1. Identify the missing general decision, not just the incident's file or symptom.
   Strengthen an existing rule when it already covers the mechanism.
2. Add a new stable rule ID only for a distinct, reusable failure pattern. Include
   **trigger, failure mechanism, required approach, authoritative owner and
   observable regression evidence**. Add its route to the selection table.
3. Update the owning implementation/guide and affected `validation.json` selectors,
   consumers or scenarios when needed. A prose reminder cannot replace the test
   or make an unselected regression part of future checks.
4. Maintain example links when code moves; update rule references when rules merge
   or retire. Do not silently reuse an ID for a different meaning. Remove obsolete
   advice rather than appending conflicting exceptions or dated status updates.

Keep this a compact set of reusable decisions. Do not add test-count histories,
commit diaries, machine-specific commands or a parallel copy of feature contracts.
Unconfirmed suspicions belong in an issue or ignored investigation notes. This
guide supports engineering judgment and executable validation; it cannot make
unreviewed generated code reliable by itself.

name: CI

on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1" # Preserve the former weekly full-health Rust run.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      diagnostic_timing:
        description: Full-workspace test-only delivery phase timings
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.run_id || 'candidate' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}

# Read-only: every job just checks out and runs tooling — nothing writes back.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Keep stack file/line diagnostics without generating type/variable debug data.
  CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only
  CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG: line-tables-only
  MESH_TALK_TEST_TIMING: ${{ inputs.diagnostic_timing && '1' || '0' }}

jobs:
  scope:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci-scope.yml

  checks:
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    needs: [scope]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # Windows uses the reusable single-build archive workflow below. Linux
      # and macOS retain complete workspace tests; macOS instruments Host only.
      # Keep compute-heavy protocol tests on Apple Silicon. Desktop browser
      # admission separately waits for Health/WebKit and bounds its fan-out.
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ needs.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && matrix.os || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: ${{ needs.scope.outputs.full }}
          upstream_result: ${{ needs.scope.result }}
      - name: Report documentation-only coverage through Codecov
        if: steps.scope.outputs.full == 'false' && matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          version: v11.3.2
          run_command: empty-upload
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          fail_ci_if_error: true
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Prepare hosted Linux build storage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        id: runner_storage
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/runner-storage.mjs --prepare | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/runner-storage.json"

      - name: Preserve runner storage measurements
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && steps.runner_storage.outcome == 'success') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: runner-storage-${{ github.job }}-${{ strategy.job-index || 0 }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/runner-storage.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Prepare Ubuntu archive source
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/ubuntu-apt-source.mjs

      # Tauri v2 system libraries (Linux only).
      - name: Install Tauri system dependencies (Linux)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest') }}
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libgtk-3-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            patchelf \
            gdb

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt, llvm-tools-preview

      - name: Cache Rust build
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          workspaces: . -> target
          key: workspace-checks
          cache-on-failure: true

      - name: Install frontend dependencies and check standards
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix frontend
          node scripts/validation/standards.mjs
          node scripts/check-repository-hygiene.mjs

      - name: Install cargo-llvm-cov and cargo-nextest
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.88.1
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov@0.8.7,cargo-nextest@0.9.150

      - name: Verify coverage accumulation with the actual tool
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        # These fixtures launch real Cargo/rustc processes and share this job's
        # package cache. Give each compiler contract exclusive execution.
        run: node --test --test-concurrency=1 scripts/ci/backend-coverage.test.mjs scripts/ci/native-host-coverage.test.mjs scripts/ci/rust-profile.test.mjs scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.test.mjs

      - name: Prepare and verify Linux native crash evidence
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e -o pipefail
          ulimit -c 262144
          node scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.mjs setup
          node scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.mjs selftest

      # Tauri reads frontendDist, so build the frontend before any Cargo step.
      - name: Build frontend
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run build

      - name: Check built JavaScript for macOS 12 WKWebView
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run check:build-syntax

      # Keep native lint, production builds and complete tests on every OS.
      - name: Clippy
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Build workspace
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: cargo build --workspace --locked

      # Linux/Windows own complete instrumented workspace coverage. macOS keeps
      # desktop-specific Host coverage (including native updater policy) and runs
      # every remaining workspace target normally, avoiding a duplicate costly
      # instrumented Core test build. No platform repeats its test suite.
      - name: Test + coverage (macOS)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (matrix.os != 'ubuntu-latest') }}
        working-directory: src-tauri
        shell: bash
        env:
          RUST_TEST_THREADS: 4
          NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS: 4
        run: |
          bash ../scripts/ci/workspace-coverage.sh macos
          # llvm-cov runs Host; Nextest runs the remaining default targets.
          # Stable Rust doctests retain their original separate check.
          cargo test --workspace --doc

      - name: Test + coverage (Linux)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest') }}
        working-directory: src-tauri
        shell: bash
        run: bash ../scripts/ci/workspace-coverage.sh linux

      - name: Workspace doctests (Linux)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest') }}
        run: cargo test --workspace --doc --locked

      - name: Multi-process core evidence and coverage (Linux)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest') }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          EVAL_OUTPUT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/backend-eval-results
          EVAL_COVERAGE: "1"
        run: |
          node scripts/evals/backend-runner.mjs
          cargo llvm-cov --no-report -p mesh-talk-core --test bridge_cross_lan -- --ignored --test-threads=1

      - name: Large-folder enqueue regression (Linux)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest') }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          large_folder_status=0
          cargo llvm-cov test --no-report --locked -p mesh-talk-core --test large_directory_enqueue large_directory_enqueue_uses_compact_manifest_instead_of_frame_error -- --exact --ignored --test-threads=1 2> "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.stderr.log" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.log" || large_folder_status=$?
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.stderr.log" >&2
          if (( large_folder_status != 0 )); then exit "$large_folder_status"; fi
          node scripts/evals/backend-runner.mjs --validate-large-folder "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.log"
          cargo llvm-cov report --lcov --output-path src-tauri/e2e-lcov.info

      - name: Preserve Linux backend evaluation evidence
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest') }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: backend-core-ubuntu-24.04-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/backend-eval-results/
          if-no-files-found: ${{ job.status == 'success' && 'error' || 'ignore' }}
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Collect Linux native crash evidence and retire its storage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        run: node scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.mjs collect

      - name: Preserve Linux native crash diagnostics
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: native-crash-linux-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/native-crash-diagnostics/reports/
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Upload test timing diagnostics
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && env.MESH_TALK_TEST_TIMING == '1') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: test-timing-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/mesh-talk-test-timing.log
          if-no-files-found: warn

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (!(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.base_ref == 'dev' && github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')) }}
        # Dependabot PRs to dev cannot read the Actions CODECOV_TOKEN secret.
        # Their tests still run; only the unauthenticated upload is skipped.
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          version: v11.3.2
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: ${{ matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && 'src-tauri/lcov.info,src-tauri/e2e-lcov.info' || 'src-tauri/lcov.info' }}
          name: workspace-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          # Branch protection requires codecov/patch; surface upload failures in CI too.
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  windows:
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    needs: [scope]
    uses: ./.github/workflows/windows-workspace.yml
    with:
      full: ${{ needs.scope.outputs.full }}
      upstream_result: ${{ needs.scope.result }}
      diagnostic_timing: ${{ inputs.diagnostic_timing || false }}
    secrets: inherit
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run from src-tauri (or a fixture workspace); preserve each platform's cohort.
set -e -o pipefail
case "${1:-}" in
    linux|macos) platform="$1" ;;
    *) echo "Usage: workspace-coverage.sh linux|macos" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
if [ "$platform" = linux ]; then
    ulimit -c 262144
else
    # Hosted ARM has 3 CPUs/7 GiB. The complete four-job cohort accumulated
    # substantial compression/swap; bound compilation independently of tests.
    # Scope admission here, after cache restore; test workers stay at four.
    export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2
fi
run_phase() {
    local phase="$1"
    shift
    if [ "$platform" = macos ] && [ "$(uname -s)" = Darwin ]; then
        # Diagnostic snapshots are not acceptance gates. time retains the actual
        # command's exit status and reports CPU time and maximum child RSS;
        # that RSS is not the peak aggregate memory of concurrent compilers.
        echo "native-resource phase=$phase"
        /usr/sbin/sysctl hw.ncpu hw.memsize vm.swapusage || echo "native-resource sysctl unavailable"
        /usr/bin/vm_stat || echo "native-resource vm_stat unavailable"
        /usr/bin/time -l "$@"
    else
        "$@"
    fi
}
run_coverage() {
    # Finish every selected case in a partition. A failed Host rejects the
    # candidate before compiling or executing another partition.
    if
        run_phase host cargo llvm-cov nextest --no-report --locked -p mesh-talk --no-tests fail --no-fail-fast --retries 0 --user-config-file none --profile default --success-output immediate --test-threads 4
    then :; else return "$?"; fi
    if [ "$platform" = linux ]; then
        if
            run_phase remaining cargo llvm-cov nextest --no-report --locked --workspace --exclude mesh-talk --no-tests fail --no-fail-fast --retries 0 --user-config-file none --profile default --success-output immediate --test-threads 4
        then :; else return "$?"; fi
    else
        # macOS instruments Host only; all remaining default targets still run.
        if
            run_phase remaining cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude mesh-talk --no-tests fail --no-fail-fast --retries 0 --user-config-file none --profile default --success-output immediate --test-threads 4
        then :; else return "$?"; fi
    fi
    run_phase report cargo llvm-cov report --lcov --output-path lcov.info
}
if [ "${MESH_TALK_TEST_TIMING:-0}" = 1 ]; then
    run_coverage 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/mesh-talk-test-timing.log"
else
    run_coverage
fi
